$comment: Input for scripts/car-model/glb-to-parts-stl.py + stl-to-glb.mjs (see .claude/skills/rally-car-import). Source: sources/cars/bimmer-gt2/1-e92-barnfind.glb (CC BY 4.0, Tushar Singh). The GLB is already model-aligned (+x left, +y up, +z nose) at true scale (wheelbase 2.737 m between the hubs: front z 0.1015, rear z -2.635; the E92's 2.76 m). The offset puts the axle mid-point at z = 0 (front hub -> physics front.z) and lifts the body for ground clearance. The atlas block is also read by livery.ts at runtime - keep them in sync by editing only here.

wheels.$comment: the wheels are separate meshes (dropped below) - nothing to cut

chartBoxes.$comment: belt-crease ledge under the quarter window (|x| 0.78 - 1.1, y 0.78 - 1.02, z -1.45 .. -0.1): its sloped triangles were on the side chart, where the ledge's tiny height range made the cell edge saw-tooth (red teeth in a light blue block, user view 2026-10-07) -> top chart, which holds the shoulder strip
same ledge along the front wing / A pillar foot (|x| 0.7 - 1.1, y 0.74 - 1.0, z 0.5 .. 1.6): white / blue teeth where the wing's sloped triangles sat on the side chart -> top chart
plate pocket walls and the small faces under the tail lamps (|x| < REAR_X): rear chart (pearl), not the side charts' red blocks

gltf.$comment: primitive -> material (first matching rule wins), by the GLB's material names. Wheels (tyre, rim, spokes, nuts, nut covers), brake discs and calipers are replaced by the game's own wheels; Logo = BMW roundels, material_30 = rear plate, Glass_Smoked = a second glass layer inside Material_806. Lamps keep their 3D geometry (housing, projector bodies, LED rings, red tail strip, covers) with shared lamp materials.

parts.$comment: the model's own bumper-lip / skirt carbon: body triangles whose (blurred) texture is dark and unsaturated, split along the texture border (refine, 2 cm). Front lip + skirts only (z): the rear corners of the original are painted, their dark texels are grime
the vent slot in each rear bumper corner (behind the rear wheel, opening backwards): its inside walls black, not livery
inside of the open rear fender flare beside each tail lamp (its flat ledge, y and z in the source's coordinates): plain white, not the livery's blocks / undercoat

solids.$comment: white back wall inside the open rear fender flare (left): the gap beside the tail lamp no longer shows through the car (frame turned 180 deg so its face looks backwards: v = -y, w = -z)
white back wall inside the open rear fender flare (right): the gap beside the tail lamp no longer shows through the car (frame turned 180 deg so its face looks backwards: v = -y, w = -z)
